doc.title: Paul Shaffer interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 24, 2023

title: Ed Sullivan Show, Canadian TV and a family trip to Las Vegas
summary: Shaffer's lawyer father and musical mother loved show business; the family watched Ed Sullivan and took him to Las Vegas at 12.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I’m sorry, there’s a nice anecdote about you going to see Nat King Cole in Las Vegas?

Okay. Well my parents were, you know my father a lawyer in this town of Thunder Bay doing all kinds of law, a specialist in civil litigation but he would do a will or an accident case you know, or even a criminal, whatever was going on. My mother a lovely housewife. Both of them very musical and totally interested in show business. And to talk about that “Ed Sullivan Show” it was a lifeline because besides the teenage acts that he presented, Ed had everybody that was anybody in show business and he made stars at that time, and we could see it on Canadian television, the CBC carried “The Ed Sullivan Show.” So that was — Sunday night was, you know, family night around the TV and everyone in the business talks about it so nostalgically. Of course it wouldn’t happen today. But Ed had something for everybody, whether it be all the old comics that I also became familiar with, the Shecky Greenes, the Myron Cohens and all of them.

He had the little Italian mouse, you see how? Yeah, who could forget this. Senor Wences — a different guy, but he had yeah this thing. Boy that left an impact. And my parents took — they were very interested in Las Vegas, hearing about it, all, so many of these performers on television and on the talk shows Johnny Carson was our only talk show host at that time. We finally got cable TV from Duluth, Minnesota and were able to see Johnny Carson. And then, you know, Las Vegas, everybody seemed to be talking about it and especially Sinatra you know, my parents’ favorite. Although my dad did turn me on to Ray Charles I must say, pretty hip for a lawyer in Northern Ontario. And then they took me as a 12-year-old kid to Las Vegas for a trip. But they didn’t gamble at all. Barely put a quarter in the machine, just wanted to see the shows.
